title: Shaft design for combined torque and bending
examples: How do I size a shaft for torque and bending?
How do I find the torque from power and speed?

explain.say: A shaft in a gearbox has two jobs at once: it twists to carry torque, and it bends under the gear push. Get the diameter wrong and it snaps. Look at our machine: a 10 kilowatt motor turns a shaft at 300 rpm, with a gear in the middle between two bearings a metre apart.

explain.say: First the twist. Torque is power over angular speed. 300 rpm is 31.4 radians per second, so T is 10,000 over 31.4, about 318 newton metres. Twisting makes a shear stress at the surface, 16 T over pi d cubed. Which part of the shaft carries the most shear?

parts.label: Gear (4 kN push)
parts.ask: Why does a gear bend a shaft?

explain.say: The outer surface. Now the bending. Treat the shaft as a beam on two supports with the 4 kilonewton gear load at mid-span. Each bearing pushes up 2 kilonewtons, and the bending moment peaks under the gear: 4 times 1 over 4, which is 1 kilonewton metre. See the triangle on the moment diagram?

Both stresses peak at the same spot, so we combine them. The maximum shear stress theory gives an equivalent torque: the square root of M squared plus T squared. Root of 1000 squared plus 318 squared is about 1049 newton metres. Bigger than either alone. Why does bending dominate here?

Because the moment is three times the torque. Now size it: with an allowed shear stress of 40 megapascals, d cubed equals 16 T e over pi times 40 million, so d is 51 millimetres. Pick a standard 55. Brilliant work! Exam tip: keyways and shoulders raise stress, so real designs add a fatigue factor.

faq.q: How do I find the torque from power and speed?
faq.a: Torque equals power divided by angular speed in radians per second. For 10 kilowatts at 300 rpm, omega is 31.4, so torque is about 318 newton metres.

faq.q: Why does a gear bend a shaft?
faq.a: The tooth force on the gear pushes sideways on the shaft between its bearings, just like a load on a simply supported beam, creating a bending moment.
A single torque that gives the same maximum shear stress as the actual combination of bending and twisting: the square root of M squared plus T squared.

faq.q: How do I size a shaft for torque and bending?
faq.a: Find the largest bending moment M and the torque T at the same section, work out the equivalent torque, then set 16 T e over pi d cubed equal to the allowable shear stress and solve for d.

faq.q: What is the maximum shear stress theory?
faq.a: Also called Tresca, it says a ductile part yields when the maximum shear stress reaches the shear stress at yield in a simple tensile test. For shafts it gives the square root of M squared plus T squared.

facts: Shaft power P = Tω, with ω in radians per second.
Shear stress from torsion in a solid round shaft is 16T/(πd³) at the surface.

quiz.say: A shaft carries 15 kilowatts at 1000 rpm. What is the torque?

wrong.1: That divides by 1000 rpm directly instead of converting to radians per second.
wrong.2: That multiplies by 60 without dividing by 2π.

quiz.say: A shaft has a bending moment of 400 newton metres and a torque of 300 newton metres at the same section. What is the equivalent torque?
quiz.show: M = 400 N·m, T = 300 N·m. Equivalent torque √(M² + T²)?

wrong.1: That simply adds them; the stresses combine by the square root rule.
